704: As I lay down my pen on this thesis, early summer is just arriving outside my window. Counting it up, this is the eighteenth year of my studies. I was born into a registered low-income household. Throughout eighteen years of schooling, support from the state and from my school has been there from beginning to end - grants arriving on time, tuition waivers actually implemented, living allowances disbursed. These seemingly procedural arrangements meant, for a child from a poor family, not having to worry about tuition at the start of every term, not having to weigh classes against making a living over and over again. I know well that being able to sit calmly in a classroom and finish these eighteen years of study rests on the strength of far too many people lifting me up. I hold that kindness in my heart.
705: I thank my parents. You are not highly educated and cannot articulate grand principles, but from childhood to now you have never once said to me, "Stop studying." In the hardest years at home, you carried all the pressure yourselves, and what you left for me was only one sentence: "You just study." Now that I am about to walk out of the school gate, looking back on the road I have travelled I have gradually come to understand that the bitterness you swallowed and the hardships you hid in those years were far, far more than I could imagine. This debt is too heavy for me to repay; I can only walk every step ahead well, so that you feel these years of sacrifice were worth it.
706: The writing of this graduation thesis has been, for me, a difficult and profound trial. Here, I wish to express my deepest gratitude and apologies to my supervisor, Teacher Wang Li. From topic selection to final draft, the thesis went through several revisions, and each draft I submitted came back covered in dense annotations. More than once I felt ashamed - the logic not rigorous enough, the expression not precise enough, the data analysis not solid enough. But Teacher Wang never rebuked me; she simply pushed the thesis back and said calmly, "Revise it again." Thinking about it now, it was precisely these repeated "revise it agains" that gradually made me understand what rigour is and what solidity is. Teacher Wang, thank you for your strictness, and thank you even more for your patience. What you taught me by word and example was far more than how to write a thesis - it was a fundamental attitude towards scholarship and towards doing things.
707: I thank every teacher who has taught me over these eighteen years. My primary school teachers taught me to read and count; my middle school English teacher did not give up on me even when I came last in exam after exam, but instead gave me special care; my university lecturers gave everything they had from the lectern. You may not remember every student, but the students remember you. It was your lessons one by one, your corrections one by one, your reminders one by one, that taught me from an ignorant child to who I am today.
708: For five years, my girlfriend Chen Shuzhuo has been by my side throughout. These five years happen to span my entire university career, and happen to be the most anxious and most confused stretch of my life. She has seen me at a loss in front of the computer, seen me silent all day because a project was stuck, and seen me pacing back and forth in self-doubt. She could not solve all my confusions, but she did not leave. Her companionship has been quiet and enduring, like a lamp that never goes out. Such affection I can only repay by treating her earnestly for the rest of my life. Writing to this page means my time as a student is drawing to a close. It would be false to say I am not confused. This identity has been with me for eighteen years, and once set down the road ahead is not yet clear. But I am not afraid because of that. Eighteen years were not easy, and since I have walked all the way here,
710: it must mean I have something in me after all - perhaps not talent, but a kind of resilience that gets back up no matter how many times it falls.
711: I believe that the late nights endured, the sweat shed and the grievances swallowed will, at some moment in the future, settle into the confidence to go forward.
712: I thank every teacher, classmate and friend I met along these eighteen years. It was the tireless teaching from the lectern, the days and nights bent over desks side by side in classrooms, the few casual words of encouragement in corridors, that paved, bit by bit, the road beneath my feet. Some people may have passed through only briefly, but I remember every kindness of those moments. I also thank the teachers who led me through the door in class, the classmates who patted me on the shoulder in the corridor, and the strangers who showed me kindness without thinking about it. You may not have noticed, but every small illumination has made me the better person I am today.
713: Graduation is not the end of the gathering, but carrying all that light with me to somewhere further away.
714: Carrying this weighty gratitude, I am willing to become a young person who is warm and steadfast, ordinary yet not mediocre, and genuinely useful to this country and this society.
715: The road is still long, but with gratitude in my heart, every step beneath my feet has somewhere it came from.
